 Mohammad Amir to enter IPL auction after securing British citizenship? 
 Former Pakistan cricketer Mohammad Amir has put an end to speculation about a possible Indian Premier League (IPL) stint after registering for the Afghanistan Premier League as a British citizen. The former fast-bowler, who acquired British citizenship earlier this year, had sparked discussions about potentially entering the IPL as a British player, similar to the route taken by former Pakistan all-rounder Azhar Mahmood.
 However, Amir has dismissed the reports, making it clear that he has no plans to register for the IPL. Taking to X, he wrote: "Hi everyone, just wanted to clarify that the news regarding the IPL is not true,"
 Amir has played 36 Tests, 61 ODIs and 62 T20Is for Pakistan and he featured in The Hundred earlier this year as a local player. He initially went unsold the players draft list as an overseas cricketer before acquiring British citizenship through his wife, Narjis Khan.
 Also Read |  Rohit Sharma set to play for Mumbai in Vijay Hazare Trophy 
 Explaining his status as a British local player, Amir had said: "I am a British local now. When you play in competitions such as the County Championship and The Hundred as a local player, you have to sign a document stating that you cannot play for another country as a local. So, the Pakistan chapter I had before is now closed,"

 For those people who can’t see Amir’s post due to geo issues, he has categorically denied the IPL news is true https://t.co/aIeUSgaasW
 — Erika Morris (@ErikaMorris79) November 2, 2026 
 Amir's registration for the Afghanistan Premier League had led to comparisons with Azhar Mahmood, who featured in the IPL between 2012 and 2015 after obtaining British citizenship. Mahmood represented Punjab Kings (then Kings XI Punjab) before also turning out for Kolkata Knight Riders.
 Pakistani players have not been allowed to participate in the IPL since the inaugural edition in 2008, making Mahmood's case a notable exception through his British citizenship.
 Amir called time on his international career after the 2024 T20 World Cup, ending a Pakistan career that spanned all three formats. Despite his retirement, the left-arm fast bowler continues to attract interest from franchise leagues around the world and remains a recognised name in T20 cricket.
